display_title: Official Review of Paper24 by Reviewer Kacf

content.summary_of_the_paper: To develop a differentiable SkewIoU-loss calculation method, this paper focuses on a novel approximate loss based on Gaussian modeling and Kalman filter. There are two main contributions: (1) For two arbitrary-oriented bounding box, convert them to Gaussian distribution, and then calculate the distribution function of the overlapping area using Kalman filter. Finally, according to KFIoU in the previous step, KFIoU loss can be calculated. (2) KFIoU loss have a similar trend with IoU loss, and also used in 3D object detection, it is a better way to realize the differentiable SkewIoU loss function. The overall and ablation experiments on several representative benchmark validates it.
content.main_review:
Strengths:
(1) Kalman filter is used in rotation object detection for the first time, and has greater improvement compared with similar methods, such as GWD. This method is an extension of the regression loss based on Gaussian distribution representation.
(2) KFIoU loss designed by the author is an effective SkewIoU loss. To calculate the SkewIoU, the authors uses Kalman filter to obtain the overlap of two Gaussian distributions.

Weaknesses:
(1) The article mentioned that the center loss provides distance information of two Gaussian distributions for KFIoU loss, but the paper does not describe, analyze or quote the relevant information of center loss.
(2) The main analysis of OpenCV and Long Edge definition methods focuses on summarizing the previous work. Authors need test their method with Long Edge definition method.
(3) This paper analyzes the advantages of the proposed method compared with GWD. KLD seems to be better than their method.

Suggestion:
(1) Compared with GWD, the effect of the proposed method is significantly improved, but it is seems lower than KLD method. The authors could provide a detailed comparative analysis between the two methods.
(2) OpenCV definition and Long Edge definition methods may have different performance for different loss designs. Therefore, the authors can do more experiments to show its effectiveness.
content.summary_of_the_review: Overall, I vote for "marginally above the acceptance threshold". I think this current submission is explained the performance of KFIoU loss in rotation object detection, and done some experiments to prove its effectiveness. However, the performance comparison and analysis of their method are not detailed enough and need to be further supplemented and modified.

replying_to: Replying to Official Review of Paper24 by Reviewer Kacf

content.title: Rebuttal to Review Kacf
content.comment:
**Q1:** The article mentioned that the center loss provides distance information of two Gaussian distributions for KFIoU loss, but the paper does not describe, analyze or quote the relevant information of center loss.

**A1:** The center loss in the article refers to the $L_{n}$ loss of the center point ($L_{c}$ in Eq. 13), not the well-known ''center loss'' in that classification field. Sorry for the misunderstanding.

**Q2:** The main analysis of OpenCV and Long Edge definition methods focuses on summarizing the previous work. Authors need test their method with Long Edge definition method.

**A2:** GWD proved that for Gaussian modeling methods, the two definitions are equivalent according to the Property1 of covariance ($\Sigma$). The experiment on the Long Edge definition will be added later.

**Q3:** This paper analyzes the advantages of the proposed method compared with GWD. KLD seems to be better than their method.

**A3:** As compared in the paper, the recent work GWD and KLD also belong to the design of regression loss based on Gaussian modeling. Compared with our work, their difference is that GWD/KLD directly uses the distance metric between distributions as the final loss. They need to be normalized with nonlinear transformation to ensure the normal convergence of model training. However, such an operation cannot truly achieve the consistency of metric and regression losses. **In this paper, we take another perspective to approximate the SkewIoU loss to better train the detector, which can be more physically coherent.**

It can be said that GWD/KLD and KFIoU are two different ideas based on Gaussian modeling. **Although we admit that the current performance of KFIoU is not as good as the improved version of GWD (KLD), we provide a brand new regression loss design perspective based on Gaussian modeling. We believe that it is inappropriate to determine the innovativeness of an article based only on performance as Reviewer L9fE does.** We believe that based on this new idea, researchers can further improve based on this work. It is worth noting that KFIoU is better than KLD on two more challenging datasets (**62.71%** vs **60.78%** in DOTA-v1.5 and **48.04%** vs **47.69%** in DOTA-v2.0), which may provide a valuable reference for subsequent further exploration.

replying_to: Replying to Official Review of Paper24 by Reviewer qdSN

content.title: Rebuttal to Reviewer qdSN
content.comment:
Thanks for your comments.

**Q1:** The motivation for using Kalman Filtering for the IoU computation is not clear.

**A1:** The main motivation is that the **current SkewIoU calculation is very complicated and cannot be directly implemented using the existing ops of the current deep learning framework. We can easily solve the above problems through approximation without the need for additional acceleration such as c++/cuda.** Many published papers are designed to be differentiable and convenient to calculate the approximate SkewIoU calculation method as a replacement regression loss:

[1] Yu Zheng, Danyang Zhang, Sinan Xie, Jiwen Lu, and Jie Zhou. Rotation-robust intersection over union for 3d object detection. In European Conference on Computer Vision, pp. 464–480.Springer, 2020a. 

[2] Zhiming Chen, Kean Chen, Weiyao Lin, John See, Hui Yu, Yan Ke, and Cong Yang. Piou loss:Towards accurate oriented object detection in complex environments. In European Conferenceon Computer Vision, pp. 195–211. Springer, 2020. 

[3] Xue Yang, Junchi Yan, Ming Qi, Wentao Wang, Zhang Xiaopeng, and Tian Qi. Rethinking rotated object detection with gaussian wasserstein distance loss. In International Conference on Machine Learning, 2021c.

In addition, we design the approximate method of SkewIoU based on Gaussian modeling because Gaussian modeling can effectively avoid the boundary problem of rotation detection, which has been explained in detail in GWD. The boundary problem of rotation detection cannot be solved simply by SkewIoU loss.

**Q2:** It is stated that the proposed new KFIoU loss function is based on Gaussian modeling of rotated bounding boxes and Kalman filter. However, the technical part of this paper did not clearly demonstrate how to use Kalman filtering techniques for IoU computation.

**A2:** The detailed process is described in detail in Section 4. Fig. 2 shows the approximate process of SkewIoU loss in two-dimensional space based on Kalman filtering. 
- Briefly, we first convert the bounding box to a Gaussian distribution as discussed in Section 3
- Move the center points ($L_{c}$ in Eq. 13) of the two Gaussian distributions to make them coincide. 
- Then, the distribution function of the overlapping area is obtained by Kalman filtering (Eq. 5). 
- Finally, the obtained distribution function is inverted into a rotating bounding box to calculate the overlapping area (Eq. 4) and the IoU (Eq. 7).

**A3:** It is confused for $V_{B1}$, $V_{B2}$ and $V_{B3}$ in Eq. (7). Are they the same as $V_B$ in Eq. (4)?

**Q3:** $V_B$ represents the voxel of a bounding box (B). $V_{B1}$, $V_{B2}$ and $V_{B3}$ in Eq. (7) refer to the three different bounding boxes shown in the right part of Fig. 2. We will add instructions to eliminate ambiguity, thanks.

content.summary_of_the_paper: This paper develops a method for calculating differentiable Intersection-over-Union loss between two rotated rectangles, named "SkewIoU" in this paper. The method uses Gaussian modeling and Kalman filter to approximate the calculation of SkewIoU. The method is tested on 2D and 3D rotated object detection tasks, including aerial image object detection (DOTA), scene text detection (ICDAR2015), and the KITTI 3-D object detection task.
content.main_review:
The motivation of this paper needs justification. The paper assumes that "SkewIoU is undifferentiable" and thus proposes a differentiable approximation to it, while to my best knowledge, there is an analytical solution to the derivative of the IoU between two rotated rectangles, as developed in [1]. Given the existence of an accurate solution, it's hard to see the reason for developing an approximation method.

[1] https://arxiv.org/pdf/1908.03851.pdf
content.summary_of_the_review: Given the aforementioned existing work, the motivation of this work needs justification.

content.title: Rebuttal to Reviewer qnDZ
content.comment:
Thanks for your comments.

First of all, **whether SkewIoU is differentiable is not exactly the same as whether it can achieve gradient backpropagation in engineering** (e.g. smooth L1). For example, the calculation of SkewIoU needs to determine whether the bounding box intersect, and how many intersection points, etc., which all cause the SkewIoU to be undifferentiable. **However, the undifferentiable part is sparse, and we can achieve gradient backpropagation in engineering.** The article you mentioned only implements the backpropagation of the gradient in engineering. It cannot prove that the SkewIoU is differentiable, and it also do not give a derivable proof process.

**As mentioned in your mentioned paper, the calculation of SkewIoU is very complicated and cannot be implemented using the ops of the existing deep learning framework. The approximate calculation we proposed can solve this problem without the need for additional acceleration such as c++/cuda.** Perhaps this should be the main motivation for my paper, and we will modify it accordingly.

We would like to give several published papers, which are designed to be differentiable and convenient to calculate the approximate SkewIoU calculation method as a replacement regression loss, to support the study of SkewIoU approximate calculation is meaningful:

[1] Yu  Zheng,  Danyang  Zhang,  Sinan  Xie,  Jiwen  Lu,  and  Jie  Zhou.    Rotation-robust  intersection over union for 3d object detection. In European Conference on Computer Vision, pp. 464–480.Springer, 2020a.

[2] Zhiming Chen, Kean Chen, Weiyao Lin, John See, Hui Yu, Yan Ke, and Cong Yang.   Piou loss:Towards accurate oriented object detection in complex environments.  In European Conferenceon Computer Vision, pp. 195–211. Springer, 2020.

[3] Xue Yang, Junchi Yan, Ming Qi, Wentao Wang, Zhang Xiaopeng, and Tian Qi.  Rethinking rotated object detection with gaussian wasserstein distance loss. In International Conference on Machine Learning, 2021c.

In addition, **we design the approximate method of SkewIoU based on Gaussian modeling because Gaussian modeling can effectively avoid the boundary problem of rotation detection**, which has been explained in detail in GWD. The boundary problem of rotation detection cannot be solved simply by SkewIoU loss.

replying_to: Replying to The KFIoU Loss for Rotated Object Detection
display_title: Official Review of Paper24 by Reviewer L9fE

content.summary_of_the_paper: The paper proposes a new loss - denoted KFIoU - for rotated object detection. The paper exploits the ideas presented in [Yang 2021c] and [Yang 2021d] where arotated bounding box is instead modelled by a Gaussian distribution, and the intersection with the ground truth at the training time is approximated by the area (volume) of the intersecting predicted and ground truth Gaussians.
content.main_review:
Rotated object detection is an interesting and important topic with many applications, and indeed the SkewIoU loss frequently used in the literature has its limitations which need to be addressed, as discussed in the paper. 

The idea to approximate a rotated bounding box with a Gaussian distribution is neat and simple, but this idea is already presented in [Yang 2021c] and then further improved in [Yang 2021d]. Even more importantly, training the Gaussian approximation using Kullback-Leibler
Divergence (KLD) as done in [Yang 2021d] seems to lead to higher accuracy on the standard datasets; yet for some reason the paper completely omits the results of KLD - for instance, using identical network architecture (RetinaNet) and training setup, on the aerial image DOTA-v1.0 dataset the proposed KFIoU loss achieves accuracy of 70.64 (Table 2), but KLD loss [Yang 2021d] achieves 71.28. I have not done thorough comparison of KLD vs KFIoU numbers on all the datasets, as I believe this should have been done in the paper, but KLD seems to consistently outperform the proposed loss where I checked (MLT, UCAS-AOD, DOTA-v1.0 datasets in Table 2)

The omission goes even further in some cases - for example for MRA-TD500 dataset (Table 5), even GWD [Yang 2021c] results are not listed (even though for other datasets GWD is included - Table 2, Table 7). The full results for AP@50, as per [Yang 2021c,d], are: Smooth L1 70.98, GWD 76.76, KLD 76.96 and KFIoU (proposed) 76.30, all using the same training setup. 

Since the KFIoU loss is the main contribution of the paper, the above issues unfortunately raise lot of questions and might leave the reader puzzled as to what is the benefit of using KFIoU vs GWD or KLD.
content.summary_of_the_review:
The paper addresses an interesting problem of training rotated object detection, but it mainly exploits the idea of approximating the bounding box with a Gaussian distribution, which was already introduced in prior work. Moreover, the prior work seems to partially or even fully on some datasets outperform the proposed method, yet these empirical results are neither included nor discussed in the paper, even though the prior work is properly referenced so the authors are aware of it.

This leaves the paper with very little contribution left, and as such I am leaning toward rejection.

**Q1:** KFIoU is not better than KLD.

**A1:** As compared in the paper, the recent work GWD and KLD also belong to the design of regression loss based on Gaussian modeling. Compared with our work, their difference is that GWD/KLD directly uses the distance metric between distributions as the final loss. They need to be normalized with nonlinear transformation to ensure the normal convergence of model training. However, such an operation cannot truly achieve the consistency of metric and regression losses. **In this paper, we take another perspective to approximate the SkewIoU loss to better train the detector, which can be more physically coherent.**

**It can be said that GWD/KLD and KFIoU are two different ideas based on Gaussian modeling.** Although we admit that the current performance of KFIoU is not as good as the improved version of GWD (KLD), we provide a brand new regression loss design perspective based on Gaussian modeling. 
**We believe that it is inappropriate to determine the innovativeness of an article based only on performance.**
We believe that based on this new idea, researchers can further improve based on this work..
It is worth noting that KFIoU is better than KLD on two more challenging datasets (**62.71%** vs **60.78%** in DOTA-v1.5 and **48.04%** vs **47.69%** in DOTA-v2.0), which may provide a valuable reference for subsequent further exploration.

**In addition, another important contribution of ours is to achieve the expansion of 3D object detection, which GWD/KLD has not done before.**


**Q2:** Figure 4 - top left and top center images in the submitted paper are identical to the Figure 2 in an arXiv preprint Yang et al, "Learning High-Precision Bounding Box for Rotated Object Detection via Kullback-Leibler Divergence" [Yang 2021d], without any attribution to the prior work
